sections.heading: Building Pad Excavation for Agricultural Structures
sections.body:
Bellhouse Excavating provides building pad excavation and subgrade preparation for agricultural structures across Brant County and Brantford. Whether the project is a new barn, a farm shop, a coverall structure, a grain bin pad, or equipment storage, the pad needs to be excavated to the right depth, properly drained, and compacted so the structure sits on a stable, long-lasting base.

Farm building pads take loads that residential foundations rarely see — heavy equipment driving onto the slab, grain weight on bin pads, livestock traffic, and seasonal moisture changes. A pad that settles unevenly, holds water against the slab edge, or was built on unstripped topsoil creates problems that are expensive to fix after the structure is up. Bellhouse handles the excavation, topsoil strip, subgrade preparation, granular base, drainage grading, and compaction so the pad is ready for the concrete contractor or building erector.

cards.title: Barn pads, coverall pads, and equipment storage buildings
cards.body: A strong fit when a new barn, coverall, or equipment storage building needs a properly excavated and graded pad. The pad is sized to the building footprint with drainage grading around the perimeter and subgrade compaction matched to the expected loads.
cards.outcome: A level, well-drained pad ready for the concrete contractor or building erector without additional excavation or subgrade correction.

cards.title: Grain bin pads and concrete ring walls
cards.body: Useful when grain bin pads need to be excavated and prepared to handle the concentrated weight of a loaded bin. The pad is excavated to the required depth, subgrade is compacted, and granular base is placed and levelled for the concrete ring wall or slab.
cards.outcome: The pad is excavated and prepared to handle the full weight of a loaded grain bin without settlement or drainage problems.

cards.title: Farm shop and implement storage pads
cards.body: A practical fit when a farm shop, implement shed, or cold storage building needs a pad excavated and prepared. The pad accounts for equipment driving onto the slab, door clearances, and drainage around the building perimeter.
cards.outcome: The pad is graded for equipment access and drainage so the shop floor stays dry and the building performs as designed.

cards.title: Pad expansions or additions to existing farm facilities
cards.body: A strong fit when an existing farm operation needs a pad added adjacent to existing buildings — a new storage bay, an equipment shelter extension, or an additional grain bin. The new pad ties into existing grades and drainage.
cards.outcome: The new pad integrates with existing site grades and drainage instead of creating conflicts with the existing buildings.

sections.heading: Farm Building Pad Excavation Includes
sections.subheading: Complete pad excavation and subgrade preparation for agricultural buildings where the loads, drainage, and site conditions require proper planning and equipment.

items.title: Site Layout & Pad Footprint Marking
items.body: The pad location is confirmed based on building plans, setbacks, access requirements, and drainage flow before any excavation begins.

items.title: Topsoil Strip & Stockpile
items.body: Topsoil is stripped from the full pad footprint and approach areas, then stockpiled on site for later use around the finished building.

items.title: Excavation to Required Depth
items.body: The pad area is excavated to the depth specified by the building plans or engineer, with the subgrade cut clean and level.

items.title: Subgrade Preparation & Compaction
items.body: The exposed subgrade is evaluated, soft spots are addressed, and the surface is compacted to provide a stable base for the granular material and slab.

items.title: Granular Base Supply & Placement
items.body: Granular A or specified base material is delivered, placed in lifts, and compacted to the required depth across the full pad area.

items.title: Drainage Grading Around the Pad Perimeter
items.body: The ground around the pad is graded to direct surface water away from the building and slab edge. Swales or drainage channels are cut where needed.

items.title: Finished Pad Ready for Concrete or Structure
items.body: The completed pad is level, compacted, properly drained, and ready for the concrete contractor to form and pour or for the building erector to begin.

factors.title: Pad size and footprint
factors.body: A larger pad means more area to strip, excavate, compact, and surface. A 30x40 shop pad is a different scope than an 80x200 barn pad.

factors.title: Topsoil depth
factors.body: Deeper topsoil means more material to strip and stockpile before the subgrade is exposed. Farm properties in Brant County can have anywhere from six inches to two feet of topsoil.

factors.title: Subgrade conditions
factors.body: A solid clay subgrade compacts well and is straightforward. Soft spots, organic material, or wet ground may need to be excavated and replaced with imported granular before the pad base can be built.

factors.title: Drainage requirements
factors.body: Pads on flat ground or in low areas need more drainage grading, swale construction, or culvert work to keep water away from the building and slab edge.

factors.title: Granular base depth
factors.body: The depth of Granular A or specified base material depends on the building loads and the engineer's specification. Grain bin pads and heavy-equipment shop pads typically need a deeper base than light storage buildings.

sections.heading: What Proper Building Pad Preparation Prevents
sections.subheading: Building pads that are rushed or poorly prepared create problems that show up after the concrete is poured and the structure is built.

items.problem: A slab that cracks and settles unevenly because topsoil was left under the pad or the subgrade was never compacted.
items.solution: Bellhouse strips topsoil cleanly from the full pad footprint and compacts the subgrade before any granular base is placed.

items.problem: Water pooling against the slab edge and seeping under the building because the surrounding grade was never shaped for drainage.
items.solution: The pad perimeter is graded to direct surface water away from the building. Swales or drainage channels are cut where the site drainage requires it.

items.problem: A grain bin pad that settles under load because the subgrade and granular base were not built for the concentrated weight of a full bin.
items.solution: Grain bin pads are excavated deeper and compacted more aggressively than standard building pads. The base depth and compaction are matched to the bin size and expected grain weight.

items.question: How deep does a farm building pad need to be excavated?
items.answer: The excavation depth for a farm building pad depends on the topsoil depth, the building engineer's specification, and the type of structure being built. Most farm building pads require the topsoil to be fully stripped — typically six to eighteen inches in Brant County — and then the subgrade is excavated to the depth needed for the specified granular base. A small equipment shelter might need eight inches of granular base while a large barn or grain bin pad might need twelve to eighteen inches or more depending on the loads. Bellhouse reviews the building plans and site conditions to confirm the excavation depth before quoting.

items.question: What's included in farm building pad preparation?
items.answer: Farm building pad preparation typically includes confirming the pad layout and footprint, stripping topsoil from the full pad area and stockpiling it on site, excavating to the required depth, evaluating and compacting the subgrade, placing granular base material in lifts and compacting each lift, grading the pad perimeter for drainage so water moves away from the building, and leaving the finished pad level and ready for the concrete contractor to form and pour. Bellhouse handles the earthwork scope — the concrete forming, pouring, and finishing is handled by a separate concrete contractor.

items.question: How much does farm building pad excavation cost in Ontario?
items.answer: Farm building pad excavation cost depends on the pad size, topsoil depth, subgrade conditions, drainage requirements, and the depth of granular base specified. A small shop pad on a site with shallow topsoil and good subgrade is a different scope than a large barn pad with deep topsoil, soft subgrade, and extensive drainage grading. Bellhouse quotes after reviewing the building plans, pad dimensions, and site conditions. Providing the building plans, pad size, and photos of the site helps Bellhouse return an accurate number.

items.question: Do you do grain bin pads?
items.answer: Yes. Grain bin pad excavation and preparation is a common project for Bellhouse across Brant County and Southern Ontario. Grain bin pads need to handle the concentrated weight of a loaded bin, which means deeper excavation, more aggressive subgrade compaction, and a thicker granular base than a standard building pad. Bellhouse excavates the pad, prepares and compacts the subgrade, places and compacts granular base, and grades the perimeter for drainage. The concrete ring wall or slab is handled by a concrete contractor after the pad is ready.

items.question: How long does it take to prepare a farm building pad?
items.answer: Most farm building pad preparation projects take one to three days of machine time depending on the pad size, topsoil depth, subgrade conditions, and granular base depth. A small shop pad on a cleared site can be completed in a day. A large barn pad with deep topsoil, soft subgrade, and extensive drainage work may take two to three days. Bellhouse confirms a realistic timeline after reviewing the building plans and site so the concrete contractor or building erector can plan their schedule around the pad completion.
